The condition to guarantee is the presence of at least one mixed-shape apple-peach pair (round apple together with pentagram peach, or pentagram apple together with round peach). Equivalently, compute one more than the size of a largest set that avoids every such pair.

All 12 watermelon candies may be included in an avoiding set, since they cannot form the required pairs. It remains only to maximize the number of apple and peach candies while forbidding both mixed pairs. The four feasible inclusion patterns and their sizes are:

- no apples (all 15 peaches) \(\to 15\),
- only round apples (all 7) together with all 9 round peaches \(\to 16\),
- only pentagram apples (all 7) together with all 6 pentagram peaches \(\to 13\),
- both apple shapes and no peaches \(\to 14\).

The maximum is therefore 16 apple/peach candies. Adding the 12 watermelons yields an avoiding set of size 28 (for example all round apples, all round peaches and all watermelons). Every 29-candy set properly contains one of the forbidden pairs, so 29 candies suffice and are necessary.

Final answer: \(29\)

The condition to guarantee is having at least one round apple and one star peach, or at least one round peach and one star apple (i.e., at least one apple-peach pair with different shapes). Let \(A_r = 7\), \(A_s = 7\), \(P_r = 9\), \(P_s = 6\), \(W_r = 8\), \(W_s = 4\).

To find the minimal \(n\) that guarantees this, compute the maximum number of candies selectable while avoiding the condition: no \(A_r\) and \(P_s\) both present, and no \(A_s\) and \(P_r\) both present. This is equivalent to \((no\ A_r\ or\ no\ P_s)\) and \((no\ A_s\ or\ no\ P_r)\), which expands to four subcases. For each, take zero from the missing types and maximize by taking all from the others:

- No \(A_r\), no \(A_s\): \(9 + 6 + 8 + 4 = 27\)
- No \(A_r\), no \(P_r\): \(7 + 6 + 8 + 4 = 25\)
- No \(P_s\), no \(A_s\): \(7 + 9 + 8 + 4 = 28\)
- No \(P_s\), no \(P_r\): \(7 + 7 + 8 + 4 = 26\)

The maximum avoiding set has size 28 (from no \(A_s\) and no \(P_s\)). Thus, 28 does not guarantee the condition, but 29 does (any selection of 29 must enter at least one crossed pair, as it exceeds the maximum in all avoiding subcases). This holds equivalently for the negation of no differing-shape apple-peach pairs (all same-shape pairs), whose max also is 28.
